text: He nailed an iron spear to the top of the church tower, in a town terrified of lightning. Then he ran an iron wire, thick as a thumb, down the wall and into the mud. The fat priest who owned the tower went pale. You're inviting lightning into my church! But he wouldn't take it down. On the other hill, his rival built a taller tower, white marble, a gold angel, and the biggest storm bell in the land. The whole market laughed at his toothpick tower, then climbed the other hill. Then the storms came. In spring, the town counted to ten between flash and thunder. The big bell rang, the storm left, and the priest smiled. See, the bell scares it off. In summer, only five. A vineyard tree split in two, and the bell ringer rang till his feet left the floor. One autumn night, they got to one. The ringer dropped his rope and ran. You see, lightning always takes the easiest road to the ground, and his iron wire was a road. One bolt ran down it, past the tower, into the wet earth. Blue flash, puff of steam, one angry chicken, the other found no road. So it smashed the gold angel, and the perfect tower burned like a candle. And the priest? He ordered a spear for every roof he owned. Even the chicken coop!
